neighbourhoods.name: Town centre and Railway Village
neighbourhoods.housing: Stone-built Victorian railway workers' cottages, flats over shops and office-to-flat conversions.

neighbourhoods.name: Old Town
neighbourhoods.housing: Georgian and Victorian houses and terraces on the hill, some split into flats.

neighbourhoods.name: Gorse Hill and Rodbourne
neighbourhoods.housing: Dense red-brick Victorian and Edwardian terraced streets, many privately let.

neighbourhoods.name: Penhill and Pinehurst
neighbourhoods.housing: Post-war council-built estates of houses and low-rise flats.

neighbourhoods.name: West Swindon
neighbourhoods.housing: 1970s and 1980s estates of terraced and semi-detached houses, such as Freshbrook, Toothill and Shaw.

neighbourhoods.name: North Swindon
neighbourhoods.housing: Large estates built from the 1990s onwards, including Abbey Meads, Haydon and Tadpole Garden Village.

neighbourhoods.name: Wichelstowe and Eastern Villages
neighbourhoods.housing: New-build estates of houses and flats still being developed on the edges of the town.

neighbourhoods.name: Highworth and Wroughton
neighbourhoods.housing: Small towns with older stone houses in the centre and post-war estates around them.

housing: Swindon grew around the Great Western Railway works, leaving a large stock of Victorian terraces near the centre, including the stone cottages of the Railway Village. Much of the town is post-war and later: council-built estates, then the large West Swindon and North Swindon developments, and now new-build villages to the south and east. Private renting is close to the national average and higher in the central terraces and town-centre flats. The town is popular with commuters to Reading, Bristol and London.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces in Gorse Hill and Rodbourne: photograph back yards, rear walls, outhouses and any damp in the back rooms.
Office-to-flat conversions in the town centre: record room sizes, windows, ventilation, fob counts and bin store access.
1970s and 1980s houses in West Swindon: check window seals, garages in blocks and shared paths and parking courts.
New-build homes in North Swindon and Wichelstowe: note snagging marks, fences, turf and any management company areas.
Railway Village cottages in a conservation area: photograph original windows, doors and stonework, as changes may need consent.
tenantHelp: Private tenants can contact Swindon Borough Council's private sector housing team about disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions.
